title: Customer commitment window calculator and risk-adjusted roadmap buckets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and CS teams repeatedly request bespoke roadmap commitments for strategic customers without a consistent way to convert signals (ACV, renewal risk, escalation frequency, technical complexity) into a standardized commitment window or treatment. That causes misaligned expectations, manual negotiation, and downstream churn on engineering priorities.

Goal: Build a lightweight decision tool and policy (the Commitment Window Calculator) that 1) ingests account signals and outputs a recommended commitment bucket (e.g., 30d SLO, 60d guarded, 90d exploratory), 2) computes a confidence score and finance-adjusted haircut to set expectation on deliverability, and 3) exposes a clear review path for exceptions. Combine this with risk-adjusted roadmap buckets that map to engineering lanes and release cadence.

Scope: MVP will include the rule engine + UI + API for Sales/CS to request a commitment recommendation, a review queue for PMs, and a short audit trail. Data sources: ARR/ACV from CRM, renewal health from RevOps, recent escalations from Support, technical complexity estimate from Solutions Engineering (SE).

Out of scope: Automated enforceable contractual amendments, contractual SLA generation, billing flows, or fully automated delivery scheduling.
acceptance_criteria: Calculator ingests ACV, renewal probability, last-12-month escalation count, and a SE complexity score and returns a commitment bucket and confidence score (0-100)
Recommendation UI available to Sales/CS with explanation text and a link to request exception review
Review queue for PMs with ability to approve/reject/modify recommendation and log rationale
Exportable audit log for compliance and quarterly OKR reporting
Benchmarked sample: on 50 historical cases, tool recommendations match historical PM decisions in >=75% of cases after tuning
comments: 2026-03-01 — Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and kickoff with RevOps, Solutions Eng, and Finance. Agreed signals list and prototype fields. Asked Engineering to estimate integration effort (ENG-42311).

2026-03-03 — Marco Li: Reviewed MVP scope; proposed simple linear scoring model (weights: ACV 40%, renewal risk 25%, escalations 20%, complexity 15%) as first iteration. Flag: we need a quick way to tune weights.

2026-03-05 — Sofia Hernandez (RevOps): Provided mapping table from CRM tiers to normalized ACV buckets; uploaded dataset for backtest (drive link below). Note: CRM data has ~6% missing fields; will supply heuristics.

2026-03-07 — Daniel Park (Finance): Requested a 'haircut' calculation tied to account payment terms — recommending conservative haircut = 15% for churn > 60 days. Added a finance check step for commitments > $250k ARR.
2026-03-09 — Marco Li: Spike complete for prototype API and UI mockups. Chose to surface both numeric confidence and an automated textual rationale (e.g., "High ACV + low complexity => 60d guarded").

2026-03-10 — Design review (Priya Rao): UI tweaks: make exception request a two-step flow; require fields: business justification + customer contacts. Also proposed color-coded buckets to make risk visible. Pending: accessibility pass.

2026-03-11 — Engineering sync (ENG-42311): Agreed on incremental rollout: backend + tests -> internal UIs -> limited pilot with 5 accounts -> broader sales pilot. Identified dependency: consistent SE complexity score (owned by ENG/SE).

2026-03-12 — Marco Li: Requested data backtest from RevOps; plan to run on last 12 months retrospectively to tune weights and produce initial KPI targets (accuracy, false positives, review override rate).
decisions: M1: Use a tunable linear scoring model for MVP rather than ML model to keep explainability for Sales and Finance
M2: Define three commitment buckets for MVP — 30d (low), 60d (guarded), 90d (exploratory) — with optional exception review for >90d
M3: Confidence score (0-100) will be required; any recommendation with <50 confidence auto-triggers PM review
M4: Finance approval required for commitments that imply >$250k ARR impact within the quarter
